subject: Stakeholder mapping & next steps — Acme Commerce evaluation
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Sophie Turner <sophie.turner@acme-commerce.com>, Victor Li <v.li@acme-commerce.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 18 Dec 2026 15:10:00 -0800
Subject: Stakeholder mapping & next steps — Acme Commerce evaluation

Hi Sophie, Victor —

Great to meet you both on the call today. Quick recap and a small ask to help us move toward a procurement-ready mutual action plan:

Recap from today's discovery (high level)
- Primary use case: realtime customer support summarization and routing for Acme's retail storefront.
- Expected peak qps: ~40 concurrent requests per region; latency target: <250ms p95.
- Data classification: PII in transcripts; retention policy: 180 days.

To unblock next steps (security & procurement), could you share a short stakeholder map — ideally: economic buyer, security contact (security engineer or manager), legal/procurement contact, and any implementation leads (SRE/Platform)? A simple org-chart or a filled version of the attached stakeholder template is perfect.

Attachments: acme-stakeholder-template.xlsx (simple CSV-style org + decision criteria)

Proposed next steps
1) Sophie: share stakeholder contacts/org chart + procurement timeline
2) We: prepare a tailored mutual action plan and a concise hosting/security summary for your security team
3) Schedule a 30-min deep-dive with your security lead (if available) next week

If it helps, I've attached a one-page mutual-action-plan we typically use for pilots — we can edit based on your timeline.

Thanks — looping in Rishi (pricing & procurement) to keep him in the loop.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0134

Hi Marissa —

Thanks for the summary and the template. Attaching a quick org snapshot below (export from our internal directory). See the key folks:

- Economic Buyer: Victor Li, VP Product (v.li@acme-commerce.com) — responsible for final budget approval.
- Security Lead: Daniel Kim, Senior Security Engineer (daniel.kim@acme-commerce.com) — handles security assessments and SOC2 evidence requests.
- Legal/Procurement: procurement@acme-commerce.com (Iris Chen) — PM for vendor contracts and SOW.
- Implementation Lead: Jenna Ortiz, Platform Eng Manager (jenna.ortiz@acme-commerce.com) — will own pilot rollout.

Procurement timeline: aiming for vendor selection and contract signature by end of Q1 2027. Procurement is expecting:
- Standard vendor questionnaire (NDA in place)
- SOC2 Type II report + recent penetration test summary
- Hosting and data residency details

I can share a short org chart (PNG) and intro to Iris if needed — would you like me to loop Iris into this thread?

Hi Sophie — thank you, this is super helpful.

Yes please, looping Iris (procurement) into the thread would be great. Quick responses to the procurement asks so we can prepare the right artifacts:

- SOC2 / pen test: we can share our SOC2 Type II report and a redacted pentest summary; Neha (cc'd) will drop the evidence pack.
- Hosting/residency: we support multi-region hosting; can confirm data residency and provide a short one-pager.

Next steps from our side
- Neha: will prepare the SOC2 evidence pack and the hosting one-pager (ETA: 48 hours).
- Rishi: I'll work with you on a draft MSA/quote aligned to Acme's estimated usage and timeline.
- Sophie: if you can introduce Iris (procurement) and Daniel (security) to this thread, we'll route the evidence + short SC-FAQ directly.

Proposed meeting: 30-min security sync with Daniel + Neha early next week (Jan 3 or Jan 4 would work from our side). Does that work for you and the team?

Thanks — attaching the mutual-action-plan again with estimated timeline for a pilot.

Best,

Looping in a couple of procurement/pricing notes to set expectations before Iris reviews the MSA:

- Pricing: we'll put together a pilot quote that includes a 6-week pilot, estimated token volumes for evaluation, and optional burst capacity. Expect a draft by next business day.
- Standard concessions: for pilots we commonly offer a limited credit + 60-day rollout SLA for support (details in draft).
- Procurement asks: Iris will likely request an executed MSA + security attestation and a draft SOW that captures hosting/residency and data handling. If Iris needs a redline-friendly MSA, we can provide a tracked (docx) draft.

Neha: once you share SOC2/Pentest summary and the hosting one-pager, I'll fold them into the draft MSA package. Sophie: please let us know Iris's preferred intake method (DocuSign vs portal + email).

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick call with procurement if that speeds things up.

Rishi
Head of Sales Operations | Redwood Inference
